title: MQTT-SN v2.0 draft packet dictionary
description: The combined output of bin/assemble_packet_dictionary.py: one entry per bytefield-backed packet, in prose order, with its byte/row structure. Written against the real assembled output (2026-10-13), not designed up front.

number.description: Display section number, e.g. '3.1' or 'C.6' (Appendix sections use a letter). Empty string when the heading has none.

order.description: Position in the spec's own prose order (bind.txt order), not alphabetical.

anchor.description: HTML/gfm-plus anchor id for this section, e.g. 'connect---connection-request'.

path.description: The full heading ancestry (level 1 first) this packet's figure sits under.

code.description: The packet type code (e.g. 'CONNECT'), split from the section title where the source uses that convention. null where it doesn't (the three Encapsulation sections, and the informative QoS -1 appendix variant) -- never invented.

description.description: The rest of the section title after the code, or the whole title when there was no code to split off.

label.description: The {#fig-...} anchor label used for [fig](#label) cross-references in the prose.

source_edn.description: Path (relative to src/) to the bytefield-svg .edn this packet's rows were derived from.

address.description: Byte offset, possibly an arithmetic expression (e.g. '4+F', '11+AM') when a preceding optional field makes it variable.

kind.description: 'gap' is a variable-length field (e.g. Client Identifier) with no fixed byte width.

annotations.description: The field's own conditional/arithmetic qualifier text, e.g. '(AM=F+1 or F) - only present when MAM flag is set', kept structured rather than mashed into the name.

group.description: The enclosing field-group title (e.g. 'Session Expiry Interval', 'Will Fields'), or null when this field isn't part of a named optional group.
The bit-field's own byte-level name (e.g. 'Connect Flags', 'Will Flags') -- always present in practice, every bit-field in the corpus has exactly one header.

value.description: The example bit pattern shown in the diagram, e.g. '0', 'X', '000', 'XX' -- one character per bit, concatenated from the diagram's per-bit value boxes.
